subject: english-literature
topicDisplay: Paper 2: Modern Drama and Literary Heritage Texts
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is chiefly concerned with analysing how a writer uses language, form and structure to create meanings and effects?
questions.explain: AO2 rewards analysis of a writer's language, form and structure using relevant subject terminology.

questions.q: Who wrote the modern drama 'An Inspector Calls'?
questions.explain: 'An Inspector Calls' was written by J.B. Priestley and first performed in 1945.

questions.q: Who wrote the modern drama 'A View from the Bridge'?
questions.explain: 'A View from the Bridge' is a play by the American dramatist Arthur Miller.

questions.q: Who wrote the literary heritage play 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explain: 'Romeo and Juliet' is a tragedy by William Shakespeare.

questions.q: Who wrote the literary heritage novel 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explain: 'Pride and Prejudice' is a novel by Jane Austen, first published in 1813.

questions.q: Who wrote the literary heritage novel 'Great Expectations'?
questions.explain: 'Great Expectations', which follows the orphan Pip, was written by Charles Dickens.

questions.q: In 'An Inspector Calls', what is the surname of the family being questioned by the Inspector?
questions.explain: The Inspector questions the Birling family about the death of Eva Smith.

questions.q: In a play script, what are 'stage directions'?
options: Instructions describing setting, movement and delivery
A long speech by a character alone on stage
The moral message of the play
The dialogue spoken between two characters
questions.explain: Stage directions are the playwright's instructions about setting, action and how lines are delivered.

questions.q: What is the poetic form of the opening Prologue spoken by the Chorus in 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explain: The Prologue ('Two households, both alike in dignity') is written as a fourteen-line sonnet.

questions.q: Which assessment objective rewards close knowledge and understanding of a text alongside an informed personal response?
questions.explain: AO1 rewards knowledge and understanding of texts and a critical, personal engagement with them.

questions.q: Which assessment objective rewards understanding of the relationships between texts and the contexts in which they were written?
questions.explain: AO4 rewards understanding of contextual factors and the relationship between text and context.

questions.q: Which best describes what is meant by a 'modern drama' text on this paper?
options: A play written and set in the twentieth or twenty-first century
A novel adapted from a modern poem
Any text by a living author
questions.explain: Modern drama refers to plays of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, distinguishing them from earlier heritage texts.

questions.q: Which best describes a 'literary heritage' text?
options: A well-established text from an earlier period regarded as part of the literary canon
A play written within the last five years
A modern novel by a living writer
A text translated from another language
questions.explain: Literary heritage texts are established works from earlier periods, including Shakespeare and nineteenth-century novels.

questions.q: What is 'dramatic irony'?
options: When the audience knows something that one or more characters do not
When a character speaks directly to the audience
When the ending is unexpectedly happy
When two characters argue on stage
questions.explain: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience possesses knowledge that a character on stage lacks, creating tension.

questions.q: What is a 'soliloquy' in drama?
options: A speech in which a character alone on stage reveals their inner thoughts
A short remark heard only by the audience while others are present
A conversation between two main characters
The playwright's written notes on staging
questions.explain: A soliloquy is delivered by a character alone on stage, sharing their private thoughts with the audience.

questions.q: In 'A View from the Bridge', what is the dramatic role of Alfieri?
options: A lawyer who acts as a narrator and chorus figure
The main antagonist who opposes Eddie
A comic servant providing light relief
questions.explain: Alfieri is a lawyer who narrates and comments on the action, functioning like a Greek chorus.

questions.q: A student explains how the 1912 setting of 'An Inspector Calls' would have prompted Priestley's 1945 audience to reflect on social responsibility. Which AO is chiefly being addressed?
questions.explain: Linking the play's setting to its historical context and audience addresses AO4.

questions.q: A student writes closely about how a writer's use of a metaphor and short, fragmented sentences creates tension. Which AO is chiefly being addressed?
questions.explain: Analysing specific language and structural choices and their effects addresses AO2.

questions.q: A student offers a well-informed personal interpretation of a character, supported by precise reference to the text. Which AO is most directly rewarded?
questions.explain: An informed personal response backed by textual knowledge is exactly what AO1 rewards.

questions.q: Eddie Carbone's fatal flaw and downfall in 'A View from the Bridge' make him best described as which type of figure?
questions.explain: Eddie's flaw leading to his destruction shapes him as a tragic protagonist in Miller's play.
